# Hear the Chart

> Hear the Chart is a free web app that turns a picture of a chart into sound, speech and an accessible table. Built for blind and low-vision people; not yet tested with screen-reader users. You photograph, upload, paste or drop a chart; Claude, Anthropic's model, reads its values; the page plays them as a melody, speaks a one-line headline, and puts every value in a table you can move through by keyboard.

## How it works

- The picture is redrawn in the browser as a JPEG and sent to Claude to read the chart's values. The site does not store or log the photo.
- The values come back as a table. Plain code on the page derives the headline, the key facts and each series' trend from that table.
- Each series plays as one continuous tone: a higher value is a higher pitch.
- In the table, Left and Right step through a series with a note and the spoken value; Up and Down change series; T speaks the trend. P plays, A plays all series, K speaks the key facts, M switches the built-in voice, Escape or Space stops.
- Verify compares the reading with data you supply (a CSV or JSON file). The file is read in the browser and never leaves the page.

## Limits

- A value that cannot be read from the picture is marked "Not known", with the reason; it is not guessed.
- Readings can be wrong. Glare, blur, small print and charts without labelled axes make reading harder. Verify against the source data when it matters.
- A reading takes from a few seconds to about half a minute, and up to a minute for large or glare-heavy photos.
- Sound uses the browser's Web Audio; speech uses the browser's built-in voice.
